title: Google DeepMind enters a new era as co-founder Demis Hassabis shifts AI role
excerpt: Observers express concern that the division has lost its independence and commercial reality has taken over
content_html:
When Sir Demis Hassabis said AI had brought the world to a “pivotal moment in human history” last month, he knew another big change was imminent.

This shift was closer to home. The Nobel prize-winning head of Google DeepMind, Google’s AI unit, announced this week he was relinquishing his day-to-day duties as chief executive and becoming chair. He is also taking on the role of chief scientist at DeepMind’s parent, Alphabet.

Hassabis and DeepMind have been key players in AI’s breakthrough era. The 50-year-old co-founded DeepMind and sold it to Google in 2014, which gave him the resources to oversee a number of advances.

These included building the AlphaGo system that mastered the Chinese board game Go and developing AlphaFold, a programme that predicts the 3D structure of proteins. The latter resulted in Hassabis being jointly awarded the 2024 Nobel prize in chemistry.

A former Google executive said the leadership overhaul showed London-based DeepMind being brought firmly into the orbit of its parent in Mountain View, California. DeepMind will now be run by Hassabis’s longstanding colleague, the US-based Koray Kavukcuoglu, who will take the non-CEO role of senior vice-president of DeepMind.

“The era of DeepMind as an independent actor is over and the obvious sign of that is you have gone from a charismatic founder-leader to appointing Koray in a non-CEO leadership role. Koray is a technical character, not an inspirational figure like Demis,” said the former executive.

The ex-Google employee added that it would be “galling” for Google and Hassabis that the latest iterations of Google’s flagship AI model series, Gemini, have lost ground to rival models developed by its US rivals Anthropic and OpenAI.

Hassabis has said he was looking forward to focusing more on the “big picture” for AI and believed he was handing over operational management of a unit that was well placed for the competitive battles ahead.

Internally, DeepMind is a workplace where there have been political tensions. Employees who spoke to the Guardian said there was internal disquiet over the company’s work with the Pentagon. Earlier this year, a former Google DeepMind employee launched a legal challenge against Google, claiming they were unfairly dismissed for their views on Gaza.

That employee was involved in unionisation efforts at Google DeepMind, which have taken place against a backdrop of concern that Google’s AI could assist militaries, including the Israel Defense Forces. Another Google DeepMind employee resigned from the company in mid-July, citing Google’s work with the Pentagon and the US Department of Homeland Security.

One said to the Guardian that Hassabis’s departure was the “end of an era”.

“Now the person we were supposed to trust to get the right outcomes for humanity has stepped away,” they said. Google DeepMind “has become just another subdivision of Google”, they added.

Rosa Curling, the executive director of Foxglove, a campaign group that supported the Google DeepMind employee in their legal challenge, said: “The departure of the co-founder of a company that once prided itself on its ethical credentials is likely to cause further concern among its frontier AI staff about how their work will end up being used in the real world.”

Google has said it is committed to the “private and public sector consensus” that AI should not be used for domestic mass surveillance or autonomous weaponry without “appropriate human oversight”. While Google has declined a voluntary union recognition agreement in London, it has said it valued “the constructive and direct dialogue that we have with our employees about building a positive and successful workplace”.

On the commercial side, a new cutting-edge model, Gemini 3.5 Pro, has yet to be released amid reports it has been delayed owing to attempts to improve its code-writing abilities – a core part of the appeal of Anthropic and OpenAI’s best products.

Google’s two AI labs, London-based DeepMind and California-based Google Brain, were merged into Google DeepMind under Hassabis’s leadership three years ago. Control now appears to be moving back to the US, where Google’s co-founder Sergey Brin is reportedly playing a bigger role in AI development.

Citing the departure of the leading AI researcher Yann LeCun from Meta and Geoffrey Hinton from Google as another example of “the end of an era in the AI ecosystem”, the former executive added: “This is very clearly a sign that the science-driven agenda of leadership in these labs has given way to cold, hard commercial reality that all of these companies want to make a return on the hundreds of billions of dollars they have invested in AI.”

The source added, however, that Google still had the benefit of being able to combine its Gemini models with an impressive suite of products, from its all-conquering search product to its cloud platform and YouTube. Thanks to its search business it also has the money to continue investing heavily in AI, having generated net income – a US measure of profit – of $132bn (£98bn) last year.

Hassabis has also taken on a more statesman-like role in recent years. The reference to a “pivotal moment” came in a blogpost in which he called for a US safety body to assess cutting-edge models, with the hope it would lead to the establishment of global standards.

The need for such a body, Hassabis argued, was pressing because the tech industry was approaching the “pivotal” point of achieving AGI, the term for a theoretical state of AI where a system can perform any human cognitive task – which also means being capable of performing white collar jobs in sectors such as law, finance and health.

A Google spokesperson said: “This is a move Demis has been thinking about for a while. He is very excited, and this will give him more time to focus on AI-driven scientific breakthroughs.” They disputed that the changes had anything to do with the performance of Gemini.

Hassabis’s move was announced alongside the departure of Jeff Dean, a veteran Google engineer and DeepMind’s chief scientist, who is leaving along with three other top researchers to form an AI startup called Discovery Loop.

According to one former Google employee, Dean’s departure could augur further personnel losses. Dean’s move also follows OpenAI’s poaching in June of Google’s Noam Shazeer, a leading figure in the field as co-author of the 2017 research paper Attention is All You Need, a crucial step in developing chatbots.

“It’s hugely problematic for Google,” said Jeremy Nixon, a former AI researcher at Google and founder of Infinity Artificial Intelligence Institute, a startup. “It’s problematic because of who Jeff will hire and because the primary reason people want to work at Google is because of him and Noam Shazeer and all these other phenomenal researchers. It’s no longer true to say that if you want to work with the greatest researchers on the planet, you go to Google DeepMind.”

Nixon added that Dean was an “angelic diplomat” who could “deal with these complex political organisations”.

Google denies it faces a post-Dean talent crisis, pointing to attrition rates for AI talent for the first half of this year being lower than they were at this time last year.

If AI is indeed facing a pivotal moment, Google has just had one.

content_html_zh:
当杰米斯·哈萨比斯爵士上个月表示人工智能已将世界带到“人类历史上的关键时刻”时，他知道另一场重大变革即将到来。

这种转变离我们的家更近了。 谷歌人工智能部门谷歌 DeepMind 的诺贝尔奖获得者负责人本周宣布，他将放弃首席执行官的日常职责，转而担任董事长。 他还担任 DeepMind 母公司 Alphabet 的首席科学家。

Hassabis 和 DeepMind 一直是人工智能突破时代的关键参与者。 这位 50 岁的人联合创立了 DeepMind，并于 2014 年将其出售给谷歌，这为他提供了监督多项进展的资源。

其中包括构建掌握中国棋盘游戏围棋的 AlphaGo 系统，以及开发 AlphaFold（一个预测蛋白质 3D 结构的程序）。 后者与哈萨比斯共同荣获 2024 年诺贝尔化学奖。

谷歌一位前高管表示，此次领导层改革表明，总部位于伦敦的 DeepMind 已被牢牢纳入其位于加州山景城的母公司的轨道上。 DeepMind 现在将由哈萨比斯的长期同事、美国的 Koray Kavukcuoglu 负责运营，他将担任 DeepMind 高级副总裁的非首席执行官职务。

“DeepMind 作为独立演员的时代已经结束，明显的迹象是你已经从一个有魅力的创始人兼领导者转变为任命 Koray 担任非首席执行官领导角色。 科雷是一个技术人物，而不是像戴米斯那样鼓舞人心的人物，”这位前高管说道。

这位前谷歌员工补充说，谷歌旗舰人工智能模型系列 Gemini 的最新迭代已经输给了美国竞争对手 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 开发的竞争对手模型，这对谷歌和 Hassabis 来说是“令人恼火的”。

哈萨比斯表示，他期待更多地关注人工智能的“大局”，并相信他正在移交一个为未来竞争做好准备的部门的运营管理。

在内部，DeepMind 是一个政治紧张的工作场所。 接受《卫报》采访的员工表示，公司内部对与五角大楼的合作感到不安。 今年早些时候，一名前谷歌 DeepMind 员工对谷歌发起法律挑战，声称他们因对加沙的看法而被不公平地解雇。

该员工参与了 Google DeepMind 的工会活动，该活动是在人们担心 Google 的人工智能可能会协助包括以色列国防军在内的军队的背景下进行的。 另一名谷歌 DeepMind 员工于 7 月中旬从公司辞职，理由是谷歌与五角大楼和美国国土安全部的合作。

一位人士对《卫报》表示，哈萨比斯的离开是“一个时代的结束”。

他们说：“现在我们应该信任的那个能够为人类带来正确结果的人已经离开了。” 他们补充道，谷歌 DeepMind“已经成为谷歌的另一个分支”。

支持谷歌 DeepMind 员工提起法律诉讼的运动组织 Foxglove 的执行董事罗莎·柯林 (Rosa Curling) 表示：“一家曾经以其道德资历而自豪的公司的联合创始人的离职可能会引起其前沿人工智能员工进一步担心他们的工作最终将如何在现实世界中使用。”

谷歌表示，它致力于“私营和公共部门的共识”，即在没有“适当的人类监督”的情况下，人工智能不应被用于国内大规模监视或自主武器。 尽管谷歌拒绝了伦敦的自愿工会认可协议，但它表示重视“我们与员工就建立积极和成功的工作场所进行的建设性和直接对话”。

在商业方面，新的尖端型号 Gemini 3.5 Pro 尚未发布，有报道称，由于试图提高代码编写能力而被推迟，而代码编写能力是 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 最佳产品吸引力的核心部分。

谷歌的两个人工智能实验室，伦敦的 DeepMind 和加州的 Google Brain，三年前在哈萨比斯的领导下合并为谷歌 DeepMind。 现在控制权似乎又回到了美国，据报道谷歌联合创始人谢尔盖·布林在美国的人工智能开发中发挥着更大的作用。

这位前高管将 Meta 的领先人工智能研究员 Yann LeCun 和谷歌的 Geoffrey Hinton 的离职作为“人工智能生态系统一个时代的终结”的另一个例子，并补充道：“这非常清楚地表明，这些实验室的科学驱动的领导议程已经让位于冷酷、艰难的商业现实，所有这些公司都希望从他们在人工智能上投资的数千亿美元中获得回报。”

不过，消息人士补充说，谷歌仍然拥有能够将其 Gemini 模型与一系列令人印象深刻的产品相结合的优势，从其无坚不摧的搜索产品到其云平台和 YouTube。 得益于其搜索业务，该公司还有资金继续大力投资人工智能，去年净利润（美国的利润衡量标准）达到 1,320 亿美元（980 亿英镑）。

近年来，哈萨比斯也扮演了一个更像政治家的角色。 他在一篇博文中提到了“关键时刻”，其中呼吁美国安全机构评估尖端模型，希望这将导致全球标准的建立。

哈萨比斯认为，对这样一个机构的需求迫在眉睫，因为科技行业正在接近实现 AGI 的“关键”点，AGI 是指人工智能的理论状态，系统可以执行任何人类认知任务，这也意味着能够在法律、金融和健康等领域从事白领工作。

谷歌发言人表示：“这是杰米斯考虑了一段时间的举措。 他非常兴奋，这将使他有更多时间专注于人工智能驱动的科学突破。” 他们质疑这些变化与双子座的表现有关。

哈萨比斯的举动是在谷歌资深工程师、DeepMind 首席科学家杰夫·迪恩 (Jeff Dean) 离职的同时宣布的，杰夫·迪恩将与其他三名顶尖研究人员一起离开，组建一家名为 Discovery Loop 的人工智能初创公司。

据谷歌一名前员工称，迪恩的离职可能预示着进一步的人员流失。 Dean 此举之前，OpenAI 在 6 月份挖走了 Google 的 Noam Shazeer，后者是该领域的领军人物，是 2017 年研究论文《注意力就是你所需要的》的合著者，这是开发聊天机器人的关键一步。

“这对谷歌来说是一个巨大的问题，”谷歌前人工智能研究员、初创公司无限人工智能研究所创始人杰里米尼克松说。 “这是有问题的，因为杰夫将雇用谁，因为人们想在谷歌工作的主要原因是因为他和诺姆·沙泽尔以及所有其他杰出的研究人员。 如果你想与地球上最伟大的研究人员一起工作，就去 Google DeepMind，这种说法已经不再正确了。”

尼克松补充说，迪恩是一位“天使般的外交官”，可以“处理这些复杂的政治组织”。

谷歌否认面临院长后的人才危机，并指出今年上半年人工智能人才的流失率低于去年同期。

如果人工智能确实面临着关键时刻，那么谷歌刚刚经历了一个关键时刻。
